report.headline: Usage projected to rise from 20.1% to 24.6% entering the EuroLeague, but the shooting-efficiency projection cannot be trusted

projection.text: The model projects a EuroLeague usage rate of 24.6%, up from a 20.1% usage rate in the 2008-09 NBA season and above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.5%.

risks.text: Despite playing heavy minutes, his source-season usage rate of 20.1% was almost exactly average for the NBA (+0.02 sd), so the jump to a projected 24.6% usage in the EuroLeague represents a larger role than he actually held in his own league.

The players who historically made this NBA-to-EuroLeague move sat 0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average, a caveat on how selective the underlying cohort is for interpreting any player's projection.

The true shooting slope of 0.534 shows only about half of a player's shooting standing typically carries across leagues, yet the model's true shooting projection is not even reliable enough to beat guessing the league mean, so no efficiency conclusion should be drawn.

His turnover rate (10.0%) and assist rate (5.7%) in the source season were already modest, and neither is covered by a EuroLeague projection in this bundle, so any expectation about playmaking under increased usage is unsupported by evidence.

strengths.text: The usage projection is built on 115 historical NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions and, unlike the shooting model, beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.3% error vs 4.3%), so it is at least informative for ranking purposes.

The fitted slope for usage rate is 0.982, meaning the model expects this player to carry over almost all of his standing relative to his league when the move happens, supporting the projected rise above the EuroLeague average.
In the source season he combined a 41.3% three-point attempt rate with a 55.2% true shooting mark over a full 82-game, 1,824-minute workload, indicating durable, high-volume perimeter production.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 20.4% to 28.7%, a span of roughly two standard deviations of EuroLeague usage (sd 4.1%), and the 95% interval widens further to 18.2%-30.9%; the model can say this player likely gains usage but cannot pin down by how much. The true shooting projection of 59.3% should not be used at all: over 367 held-out transitions the model's error (4.7%) is no better than simply predicting the league mean (4.7%), so that metric carries no information here.
